title: Start your first excavation
keywords: getting started tutorial progression book journal help

sections.title: Start here
paragraphs: Hatch a Sniffer and expose ancient debris. Bring its artifact to an Archaeology Table. Uncover a component, then use a Reconstruction Table to assemble equipment.

sections.title: Find a relic
paragraphs: Start with a Sniffer. Expose ancient debris on a walkable surface for it to investigate. Its finds lead to artifacts and, occasionally, a Cruncher egg.

sections.title: Rebuild
paragraphs: Use the Archaeology Table to excavate finds, then the Reconstruction Table to assemble components. Your excavation quality affects every modifier that the component contributes.

sections.title: Navigation
paragraphs: Choose a category or search from any page. Articles have named sections: read the overview first, then open details when you need them. Back returns to your previous search or article.

sections.title: Your values
paragraphs: This book contains general knowledge. Your item tooltips show the values actually rolled on your own components and tools. Unread ancient runes stay hidden until you unveil them.

title: Using this field guide
keywords: controls search keyboard navigation pages

sections.title: Get a book
paragraphs: Craft a normal book with one paper for the Workshop Manual, or find it in the creative tab. Item pictures identify the subjects in Contents, entry lists, search results and article headings.

sections.title: Browse
paragraphs: Home opens the Manual's contents. Categories cover creatures, artifacts, excavation, equipment and customization stations. Modifiers opens a topic index.

sections.title: Search
paragraphs: Search looks through the whole guide, including descriptions and modifier IDs. All words must match. Clear empties search. Arrows and the mouse wheel turn pages. Select a named section to read details. Related opens connected articles; Back restores your previous view.

sections.title: Close / return
paragraphs: Escape or the close button closes the book. Reading never consumes the book, changes equipment or rolls an artifact. The last page and search are remembered during the current play session.

sections.title: Tool values
paragraphs: Hover a reconstructed tool and hold Shift while scrolling to browse its modifier pages. Effective values and grades remain on the tool; definitions and rules live here.

title: Sniffers and ancient debris
keywords: sniff ancient debris netherite scrap cruncher egg

sections.title: Raise one
paragraphs: Brush suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins to find a vanilla Sniffer egg. Hatch it and raise the Sniffer. Adults can investigate exposed ancient debris on a walkable surface; buried debris is not a target. Adults breed with torchflower seeds.

sections.title: Debris
paragraphs: When the Sniffer successfully digs at exposed ancient debris, that debris breaks and yields netherite scrap and an artifact. Mob griefing must allow the interaction.

sections.title: Egg chance
paragraphs: There is also a one-in-fifteen chance of a Cruncher egg from this excavation. Ordinary Sniffer digging still has its normal uses.

sections.title: Head drop
paragraphs: Adult sniffers drop a Sniffer Head when killed. The head is a decorative trophy, with wall attachment and sixteen floor rotations.

title: The Sniffer Head
keywords: skull head trophy wall rotation

sections.title: Get a head
paragraphs: The Sniffer Head is a decorative drop from a killed Sniffer. It is also in the creative menu.

sections.title: Placement
paragraphs: Place it on a wall to face directly out from the supporting surface. Floor placement supports sixteen rotations, including diagonals. The back sits flush against its support.

title: Crunchers
keywords: nether mob jaws wither rose food breeding

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Cruncher is a Nether relative of the Sniffer, with heavy jaws suited to breaking ancient geodes. Hatch its egg to raise one, or use the creative spawn egg for testing.

sections.title: Geodes
paragraphs: Crunchers approach geodes from beside the block and crunch them with their jaws. The geode is consumed and produces an artifact; it is not a block the player must stand the Cruncher on.

sections.title: Food
paragraphs: Crunchers eat wither roses. Their visual design uses obsidian, Nether colors and animated magma veins.

sections.title: Infection
paragraphs: An infected Cruncher has its own sculk transformation and attached parasite appearance. Further specialized infected behavior is planned.

title: Hatching a Cruncher egg
keywords: hatch incubation warped nylium magma lava stages

sections.title: Find an egg
paragraphs: A Cruncher egg can be found when an adult Sniffer excavates exposed ancient debris. Its chance is one in fifteen.

sections.title: Hatch time
paragraphs: The placed egg progresses through three visible stages. Normal hatching takes about twenty minutes, plus small random stage delays, matching the normal Sniffer egg timing.

sections.title: Speed boost
paragraphs: Place the egg on warped nylium to reduce the base hatching time to about ten minutes. It does not use the Sniffer egg moss boost.

sections.title: Clear space
paragraphs: The final hatch needs clear space for the baby. If the baby would collide, the egg waits and retries instead of losing the hatchling.

title: Ancient geodes
keywords: ominous vault trial chamber geode obsidian rare

sections.title: Vault reward
paragraphs: Ancient geodes are obsidian-like relics found as an additional reward from Ominous Vaults. The current extra-geode chance is twenty percent.

sections.title: Use a geode
paragraphs: Place one where a Cruncher can walk up to it. The Cruncher crunches the geode and releases an artifact suitable for the Archaeology Table.

sections.title: Rarity limits
paragraphs: Geodes and Sniffer debris finds are different artifact sources. Neither source currently supplies Legendary or Unique artifacts; acquisition for those rarities is reserved for later progression.

title: Sculk parasites
keywords: skulk sculk parasite infection infected hostile deep dark ancient city sensors cow zombie panda llama iron golem infected animals mobs

sections.title: Spawning
paragraphs: Sculk parasites naturally appear in the Deep Dark and Ancient Cities. Natural spawn checks keep their local population sparse. Their movement does not continually trigger sculk vibrations.

sections.title: Infection
paragraphs: A parasite jumps onto a supported mob and merges with it. Players cannot be infected. Infected hostile mobs are more dangerous and reward more experience; normally passive hosts become hostile.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: The transformation preserves the host's normal identity and applicable texture variants while adding sculk growth, an attached parasite and animated infection details.

sections.title: Excluded mobs
paragraphs: Bosses such as the Ender Dragon are excluded. So are tadpoles, ghasts and happy ghasts, endermites and silverfish, ordinary fish, squid and glow squid, bats, allays and vexes.

sections.title: Other hosts
paragraphs: Slimes, magma cubes, blazes, breezes and shulkers remain supported. Sniffers and Crunchers use specialized infected visuals.

title: Artifacts and rarity
keywords: rarity common uncommon rare epic legendary unique drop chances

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Artifacts are sealed specimens containing an ancient find in a rock matrix. A Sniffer or Cruncher can recover them. The Archaeology Table reveals the find through a cleaning minigame.

sections.title: Six rarities
paragraphs: The six artifact rarities are Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary and Unique. Rarity affects available modifiers, the odds of stronger value tiers, modifier-count attempts and scaling grades.

sections.title: Roll chances
paragraphs: A higher rarity offers better opportunities, not a guaranteed perfect component. Every modifier family has its own tier bands and rarity weights. Each modifier entry lists those weights.

sections.title: Find chances
paragraphs: Current Sniffer finds: seventy percent Common, twenty-five percent Uncommon and five percent Rare. Cruncher geode finds: eighty percent Rare and twenty percent Epic.

sections.title: Future tiers
paragraphs: Legendary and Unique acquisition is reserved for later progression. They are available in creative mode. This guide does not add drop chances for them.

title: Rock matrices and hidden finds
keywords: sandstone shale deepslate basalt obsidian stone matrix rocks

sections.title: Rock types
paragraphs: Artifacts may be encased in sandstone, shale, deepslate, basalt or obsidian. Harder matrices need more clearing and put more emphasis on the right tool for each layer.

sections.title: Hardness
paragraphs: Rarer specimens favor tougher matrices. The rock is a shell around the find; its material is not the same thing as a Nether or End influence.

sections.title: Hidden finds
paragraphs: Potential recovered finds include pickaxe head pieces, a connector, a handle, other equipment heads and blades, resonant cores and salvage materials.

sections.title: Stable rewards
paragraphs: Once a specimen is sealed, its study is stable. Completing an excavation and claiming the reward does not let you repeatedly reroll the same find.

title: The Archaeology Table
keywords: archeology archaeology excavation minigame recover extract artifact inventory field kit

sections.title: Workbench
paragraphs: This two-block workbench holds an artifact and four field tools: drill, brush, hammer and magnifying lens. Items stored in it appear physically on the tabletop.

sections.title: Load a find
paragraphs: Put an artifact in the artifact slot. Switch to the excavation workspace for a large view of the encased find. The inventory view is still available for moving tools and rewards.

sections.title: Hold a tool
paragraphs: Pick up a tool from the field kit and click or drag over the specimen. Clicking another tool returns the held tool to its proper position and switches to the new one.

sections.title: Clear rock
paragraphs: Clear the covering rock while preserving the inclusion. Thick crust calls for the hammer or drill; loose material near the find is safer to brush. The lens helps identify hidden material.

sections.title: Recover
paragraphs: When the table says Ready to recover, use Recover with the output slot empty. Take the recovered component before starting another reward. Table contents persist when the screen is closed.

title: Choosing excavation tools
keywords: drill brush hammer lens magnifying glass tools damage condition

sections.title: Drill
paragraphs: Drill: precise removal for working through cover. Use care near delicate material.

sections.title: Brush
paragraphs: Brush: gentle cleaning of loose sediment, suited to exposed edges and the final pass.

sections.title: Hammer
paragraphs: Hammer: broad removal of thick crust. Efficient for hard cover and risky near the inclusion.

sections.title: Lens
paragraphs: Magnifying lens: inspection that helps reveal where material lies beneath the surface without removing that cover.

sections.title: Technique
paragraphs: Tool choice, covering thickness and how close you are to the find matter more than simply repeating the same action everywhere. Damage reduces the recovered quality.

sections.title: Tool recipes
paragraphs: An ordinary Minecraft brush is the basic brush. The custom drill, hammer and lens recipes are listed on the following pages.

title: Field-tool upgrades
keywords: precision resonant field tool smithing upgrade diamond netherite scrap

sections.title: Three tiers
paragraphs: Field tools have basic, precision and resonant versions. Upgrades improve excavation control, speed, tool durability and inspection behavior.

sections.title: Upgrading
paragraphs: Precision upgrades use recovered components or fragments and diamonds. Resonant upgrades use resonant cores and netherite scrap. Use the smithing upgrades appropriate to the tool.

sections.title: Keeps data
paragraphs: Upgrading preserves the tool's custom name, damage and enchantments. The drill, brush, hammer and lens retain their distinct jobs at every tier.

title: Quality and scaling grades
keywords: score quality extraction excavation grade scaling f d c b a s 0 50 100 120 percent

sections.title: Quality
paragraphs: A recovered component remembers its excavation score. That score multiplies each numeric modifier on that component: a +10% mining-speed roll at 50% quality contributes +5%.

sections.title: Restoration
paragraphs: Original excavation provenance stays recorded. Component restoration can improve current quality up to 120%. At zero quality, a component grants no modifier effect.

sections.title: F-S grades
paragraphs: F, D, C, B, A and S are scaling grades. They are independent of base value tier and influence. A high base roll and strong grade work well together.

sections.title: Ascension
paragraphs: Numeric grade growth per ascension is F +6%, D +10%, C +15%, B +22%, A +32%, S +45%, relative to that modifier's quality-adjusted base. Growth adds; it does not compound.

sections.title: Level gains
paragraphs: An ordinary level selects one to three numeric contributions for a small grade-based increase. Per selected level: F 0.05%, D 0.10%, C 0.15%, B 0.25%, A 0.35%, S 0.50% of base.

sections.title: Perk stages
paragraphs: Milestone perks gain stages instead of meaningless numeric bonuses. Stages unlock at ascensions 4/7/10 for F/D, 3/6/9 for C/B and 2/5/8 for A/S.

title: Reconstructing equipment
keywords: reconstruction table crafting pickaxe sword axe shovel hoe mace spear pieces connector handle

sections.title: Patterns
paragraphs: Use the Reconstruction Table to select an equipment pattern, place its matching recovered pieces and assemble the result. Each selected pattern shows the parts it requires.

sections.title: Pickaxe parts
paragraphs: A pickaxe uses three top pieces: left tip, head bridge and right tip. Beneath them sit a connector and handle. All five pieces keep their individual scores and modifier records.

sections.title: Other tools
paragraphs: Sword, axe, shovel, hoe, mace and spear patterns are also available. Handles and connectors use universal modifiers that work on all reconstructed tool types.

sections.title: Saved data
paragraphs: The finished tool keeps each part's quality, saved rolls and customization provenance. Repeated contributions combine up to their relevant caps.

sections.title: Mining focus
paragraphs: The pickaxe has the developed mining modifier and progression system. Further specialized modifiers for other equipment can be added later.

title: The Ruined Ancient Forge

sections.title: Tier one
paragraphs: The Ruined Ancient Forge is the first, small form of the ancient workshop. Complete its masonry to reconstruct equipment with the same recovered parts and patterns as the Reconstruction Table. It does not grant extra modifier rolls or change your pieces.

The hearth holds five input pieces and an output. Completing the frame automatically forms one weathered stone-and-bronze forge. Right-click the hearth or any formed section to open it. Breaking a section restores the surviving original masonry and keeps the stored pieces safe. Breaking the hearth drops its inventory and the hearth itself.

sections.title: Ancient alloying
paragraphs: Open the completed forge and select Alloy in the upper bar. Place one Netherite Scrap or Ancient Debris in Scrap, one gold ingot in Gold, and two iron ingots in Iron. Press Alloy to make four Ancient Ingots. Ingredients and output can stack. Shift-click routes ingredients to their matching input.

Both forge modes share stored slots. Switching to Alloy preserves all your parts; remove them, including the two stored-parts slots, before alloying. Collect the result before assembling equipment. Breaking the frame blocks both modes and preserves everything inside.

sections.title: Build it
paragraphs: The footprint is three blocks wide and three deep, four blocks tall including the foundation. The hearth sits at the center of the front edge, one block above the foundation. All layers below are read front row first. B is Ruined Forge Bricks, H is the hearth, and a dot is empty space.
Foundation: BBB / BBB / BBB. Hearth level: .H. / B.B / BBB. One above the hearth: ... / B.B / .B. Two above the hearth: ... / ... / .B.

Use one hearth and eighteen Ruined Forge Bricks. The two side pillars are behind the hearth; the chimney is centered at the back. The frame rotates with the hearth. The completed structure forms a connected work pad, firebox, supports and chimney.

sections.title: Ghost layout
paragraphs: Right-click an incomplete hearth with an empty hand, then choose Show ghost layout. Translucent cyan blocks mark missing masonry. Amber marks spaces occupied by another block: clear those spaces before placing bricks. The preview never places or consumes blocks.

Click the incomplete hearth again to hide the layout. Only you see your preview, and it disappears when the forge forms or you leave the world. Shift-right-click the hearth with an empty hand to inspect repair status.

sections.title: Find or craft
paragraphs: Small ruined workshops occasionally generate in plains, forests, taigas and savannas in newly generated terrain. A found workshop contains a removable hearth and most of its frame, with two bricks missing. Repair it there or take the materials home.

Exploration is optional. Craft the same hearth from four Ruined Forge Bricks, two copper blocks, two iron ingots and one blast furnace. Forge bricks use ordinary stone crafting materials. No egg, boss drop, vault, new structure or rare random find is needed for the crafting route.
Packs can replace these recipes, change the masonry tag, or disable/add structure biomes with datapacks. The locator command is /locate structure examplemod:ruined_ancient_forge.

sections.title: The future workshop
paragraphs: This is a weathered starter forge. Advanced functions, Forgemaster rewards and future forge designs remain separate work. The planned expanding, Blood Magic-inspired structure will be the Ancient Anvil. Its exact layout and upgrades are not part of this first forge.

keywords: ruined ancient forge hearth multiblock tier one structure repair bricks craft workshop ghost preview layout formed connected

title: Ancient metal and alloying

sections.title: Make ancient metal
paragraphs: The repaired Ruined Ancient Forge can alloy ancient material with ordinary metals. Select Alloy in the forge, then use one Netherite Scrap OR Ancient Debris, one gold ingot, and two iron ingots to make four Ancient Ingots. No fuel or additional structure is needed for this first alloy.
Netherite Scrap is the vanilla scrap obtained by smelting Ancient Debris. Both forms are accepted directly. Artifacts, recovered component pieces, and Ancient Fragments are not alloy ingredients.

sections.title: Store and craft
paragraphs: Craft nine Ancient Ingots into a Block of Ancient Metal. Craft a block back into nine ingots. Three blocks and four ingots make one Ancient Anvil, following the ordinary anvil crafting shape.

The alloy screen has separate Scrap, Gold, Iron and output slots, plus two preserved-part slots. It refuses to consume ingredients when the recipe is incomplete, the output will not fit, or old parts remain stored.

keywords: ancient ingot metal block alloy smelt scrap netherite debris gold iron forge

title: The Ancient Anvil

sections.title: Build the anvil
paragraphs: The Ancient Anvil is a rune-carved metal anvil with warm inlays. Craft it like an ordinary anvil: three Blocks of Ancient Metal across the top, one Ancient Ingot in the middle, and three ingots across the bottom. This uses 31 ingots in total.

Place the anvil on its own to establish Tier 0. It is a stationary workshop structure and does not fall like a vanilla anvil. Its foundation is a separate project from repairing the Ruined Ancient Forge.

sections.title: Tier 1 foundation
paragraphs: Build a complete 3 by 3 square of metal blocks directly one layer below the anvil, centered on it. All nine blocks are required, including the center. Iron, gold, copper, netherite and ancient metal qualify; you may mix them. Diamond, emerald and lapis blocks are not metal.

The anvil automatically becomes Tier 1 when the foundation is complete. Removing or replacing a required metal downgrades it to Tier 0. The metals remain normal blocks and are never consumed. Breaking or relocating the anvil leaves its foundation in place.

sections.title: View the foundation
paragraphs: Right-click the anvil with an empty hand to see its tier and metal count. Show foundation guide displays the missing layer: cyan for air and amber for a wrong block that needs replacing. Only you see the guide. It clears when Tier 1 is complete or you leave the world.
Tier 0 and Tier 1 establish the first stages of the planned growing ancient workshop. Later tiers, rituals and artifact-modification powers will be added separately.

keywords: ancient anvil tier 0 tier 1 metal foundation multiblock blood magic ritual guide ingot

title: The reconstructed pickaxe
keywords: mining core speed efficiency fortune area crouch pickaxe

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A reconstructed pickaxe combines the three mining head pieces with a universal connector and handle. A carefully assembled build can substantially outperform an enchanted vanilla pickaxe.

sections.title: Core speed
paragraphs: The innate mining multiplier is 1 plus twice the average quality of its three head pieces. Heads at 50% give 2x native speed; 100% gives 3x; 120% gives 3.4x. This multiplies native Efficiency and Haste too.

sections.title: Resonance
paragraphs: The pickaxe has a 200-point resonance store. Primary mining and holding the tool generate quality-scaled core charge. Dedicated generation modifiers support more simultaneous spenders.

sections.title: Area mining
paragraphs: Crouch to enable area-mining perks. Native extra breaks consume durability, respect cancellation and share a limit of 64 extra blocks within a loaded 16-block range.

sections.title: Extra breaks
paragraphs: Extra breaks cannot recurse, farm tool XP or generate primary bonuses or resonance. Native Fortune, Silk, furnace handling and pure material conversions still compose with secondary loot.

sections.title: Blink controls
paragraphs: Recoil uses right-click air for a backward blink. Chorus uses sneak-right-click air for a forward blink. Both require a safe destination.

title: Tool levels and mastery
keywords: levels experience xp mastery level 100 gates

sections.title: Gain XP
paragraphs: Valid Survival or Adventure pickaxe mining grants tool XP. Creative mining, canceled breaks, incorrect-tool targets and secondary area breaks do not farm levels.

sections.title: Level gates
paragraphs: The pickaxe levels from 1 to 100. Every tenth level is an ascension gate: collect its materials and ascend before gaining more tool XP. XP at an unpaid gate is not banked.

sections.title: Level bonuses
paragraphs: Ordinary levels award small grade-scaled bonuses to one to three numeric contributions. Level-up sound marks a successful gain. Milestone perks advance with ascensions.

sections.title: Mastery
paragraphs: At full mastery, the Rally Mining modifier converts its extra tool-XP opportunity into player XP and resonance, so that investment remains useful.

title: The Ascender
keywords: ascender ascend materials resources level gate

sections.title: Use Ascender
paragraphs: The prototype Ascender has a tool slot and storage for the materials required by that tool's modifiers. Place the pickaxe at a ten-level gate and supply every listed resource.

sections.title: Costs
paragraphs: Each rolled modifier occurrence has a resource binding. Cost increases with the upcoming ascension number. Repeated modifiers and materials combine into the total requirement.

sections.title: Growth
paragraphs: Once every cost is present, the tool ascends and the exact materials are consumed. Ascension raises numeric contributions according to their grades and may unlock perk stages.

sections.title: Availability
paragraphs: This prototype has no crafting recipe. Its final late-game construction is reserved for future progression. It is available in creative mode.

title: Reading modifiers and value tiers
keywords: modifiers affixes rolls tiers tier weights rarity prefixes suffixes

sections.title: Roll process
paragraphs: A modifier family is selected by its relative weight. Then rarity weights select one of that modifier's value tiers, followed by a value within that band. Different families may have different numbers of tiers.

sections.title: Value tiers
paragraphs: T1 is the strongest value tier. Common artifacts favor low bands, with occasional stronger results where allowed. High rarities favor stronger bands and have more chances to add extra modifiers.

sections.title: Properties
paragraphs: Value tier, F-S scaling grade, excavation quality and influence are separate properties. Your tooltips show your actual values; each modifier's book entry explains its operation, limits and tier bands.

sections.title: Part roles
paragraphs: Handles and connectors roll the universal pool. Mining head pieces roll mining effects. Some harvest effects exclude each other on one piece, and Silk Touch takes priority over Fortune and furnace loot.

sections.title: Limits
paragraphs: Fortune contributions add above a native Fortune enchantment up to X. Applicable mining-XP bonuses add up to +2000%. Conditional mining-speed bonuses add up to +800%, then multiply the core and general speed bonus.

sections.title: Reference
paragraphs: The Modifiers category contains all 120 definitions. Use its topic filter for speed, loot, area mining, resonance, survival, universal parts or either influence.

title: Resonance and combinations
keywords: resonance battery charge energy combo synergy

sections.title: Energy store
paragraphs: Resonance is energy stored on an assembled pickaxe, with a capacity of 200. The innate core supplies quality-scaled charge on primary breaks and periodically while held.

sections.title: Generate
paragraphs: Battery modifiers add charge from activities such as gem mining, movement, furnace processing or trading some current mining XP. They can support multiple spenders.

sections.title: Spend
paragraphs: Spenders provide effects such as area excavation, Haste, repair, bonus loot, teleportation and protection. Each effect has its own cost, conditions and cooldown.

sections.title: Shared costs
paragraphs: Consumers share the same store and run in a defined mining-event order. If one spends the remaining energy, another may have to wait. Entanglement can refund part of spending and share that refund with nearby allies.

sections.title: Safety limits
paragraphs: Secondary breaks and remote collection cannot recursively farm resonance. Read individual modifier entries for stage values and exact conditions.

title: The Influencer
keywords: nether end influence influencer permanent themed smelting phasebound teleport

sections.title: Assign
paragraphs: Components start without an influence. The Influencer assigns Nether or End influence once and rerolls eligible modifiers with a stronger matching theme.

sections.title: Weights
paragraphs: Matching themed modifier families have sixfold relative weight. Other-influence families are excluded. Neutral families remain available, and influence-exclusive families require their matching influence.

sections.title: Permanent
paragraphs: An influence is permanent. You cannot remove it, switch it or keep applying the same influence to fish for better rolls. Annulment does not reset that rule.

sections.title: Name colors
paragraphs: Nether names have an ember-colored pulse; End names have a violet shimmer. Inventory icons keep their original appearance. A piece's individual influence is retained when assembled.

sections.title: Availability
paragraphs: Influence changes roll eligibility and weighting, not the meaning of its original excavation score. This prototype has no crafting recipe and is available in creative mode.

title: The Unveiler and ancient runes
keywords: ancient runes hidden unveil three choices reveal

sections.title: Hidden mod
paragraphs: Epic and higher components may carry a hidden ancient modifier written as unreadable runes. It replaces a modifier slot rather than adding unlimited extra rolls.

sections.title: Three choices
paragraphs: The Unveiler shows three fixed legal choices. Each choice includes a modifier, scaling grade and base value. Select one to reveal it on the component.

sections.title: Saved choices
paragraphs: The choices are saved, not freshly rerolled every time the menu opens. Revealing consumes the hidden slot. Role pools, rarity, exclusivity, influence and existing modifiers still constrain the choices.

sections.title: Restrictions
paragraphs: The Unveiler acts on recovered pieces, not assembled tools. Corrupted components cannot be modified. The prototype has no crafting recipe.

title: The Anuller
keywords: anuller annuller annul annulment remove modifier

sections.title: Remove one
paragraphs: The Anuller randomly removes one unlocked modifier from a recovered component. It cannot target a permanently locked modifier.

sections.title: Restrictions
paragraphs: It does not remove influence or make influence assignment repeatable. A corrupted component is terminal and cannot be annulled.

sections.title: Availability
paragraphs: This prototype works on pieces, not assembled tools, and has no crafting recipe.

title: The Locker
keywords: lock locked permanent protect

sections.title: Protect one
paragraphs: The Locker permanently protects one revealed modifier on a component. It cannot be removed by the Anuller or targeted by modification operations that respect the lock.

sections.title: Permanent
paragraphs: You may lock only one modifier. You cannot move that lock to a different modifier later. Hidden ancient runes must be unveiled before locking a revealed choice.

sections.title: Other actions
paragraphs: Influence assignment preserves a compatible lock and rejects a conflicting assignment. Corruption never selects the locked modifier as a target.

sections.title: Availability
paragraphs: The prototype has no crafting recipe and works on recovered pieces.

title: The Scaling Randomizer
keywords: randomizer scaling grade reroll F D C B A S

sections.title: Reroll grades
paragraphs: The Scaling Randomizer rerolls scaling grades on the component's unlocked modifiers. It does not reroll the base values, value-tier provenance or excavation score.

sections.title: Restrictions
paragraphs: A locked modifier retains its grade. Corrupted pieces cannot be randomized. Influence remains permanent and unchanged.

sections.title: Availability
paragraphs: The prototype has no crafting recipe and works on recovered pieces.

title: The Restorer
keywords: restorer restore restoration quality extraction 120 percent

sections.title: Up to 120%
paragraphs: The Restorer improves a recovered component's current quality in ten-point steps, up to 120%. Quality above 100% strengthens contributions that have room below their caps.

sections.title: Saved data
paragraphs: The original excavation score remains recorded. Restoration does not reroll its modifier families, values, tiers, grades or influence.

sections.title: Before corrupt
paragraphs: Corruption prevents further restoration. Restore a piece before taking that final gamble. This prototype has no crafting recipe.

title: The Corruptor
keywords: corrupt corruption sculk final gamble good bad outcomes

sections.title: Final gamble
paragraphs: Corruption is a final gamble on a recovered component. Once corrupted, no more component modifications are allowed.

sections.title: Outcomes
paragraphs: Possible outcomes include strengthening or weakening an unlocked modifier, raising or lowering a scaling grade, adding or removing an eligible unlocked modifier, restoring or damaging quality, or leaving the piece otherwise unchanged.

sections.title: Restrictions
paragraphs: Only eligible outcomes are rolled. Locked modifiers cannot be selected. Quality limits, modifier limits, role pools and permanent influence rules still apply.

sections.title: Plan ahead
paragraphs: Plan your restoration, revelation, influence and lock before corrupting. The prototype has no crafting recipe. Further sculk-related progression is planned.
